## Pull request overview Fixes console record detail pages when navigating via URL by normalizing `recordId` (stripping the `objectName-` prefix) so backend lookups succeed, and adds a clear empty state when a record loads as `null`. **Changes:** - Strip `objectName-` prefix from URL `recordId` once in `RecordDetailView` and reuse `pureRecordId` across DetailView, presence, comments, and edit callbacks. - Add a “Record not found” empty state to `DetailView` when loaded data is `null`. - Update/add tests covering recordId stripping and the new not-found state. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx | Adds a “Record not found” empty state after loading when data is missing. | | packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/DetailView.test.tsx | Adds tests validating the not-found empty state and optional back behavior. | | apps/console/src/components/RecordDetailView.tsx | Introduces `pureRecordId` and threads it through detail schema, presence, comments, and onEdit. | | apps/console/src/__tests__/RecordDetailEdit.test.tsx | Fixes selectors and asserts `findOne` is called with stripped/non-stripped IDs. |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (3) **packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:240** * The "Record not found" branch is triggered by a broad falsy check (`!data`). This will also render the not-found state when `data` is still `undefined` (e.g., misconfigured schema with no `resourceId`/dataSource), not just when `findOne` explicitly returns `null`. Consider checking `data === null` (and optionally `schema.resourceId` present) so only a true not-found result shows this state. ``` if (!data && !schema.data) { return (

Record not found

The record you are looking for does not exist or may have been deleted. ``` **apps/console/src/components/RecordDetailView.tsx:58** * `dataSource.find` is being called with `$filter` as an interpolated string. In `@object-ui/types`, `QueryParams.$filter` is defined as an object/AST, and the ObjectStack adapter converts object filters to an AST; passing a string can be mis-parsed (e.g., treated as a list of characters). Use an object filter like `{ recordId: pureRecordId }` / `{ threadId }` instead of a string expression. ``` // Fetch record viewers dataSource.find('sys_presence', { $filter: `recordId eq '${pureRecordId}'` }) .then((res: any) => { if (res.data?.length) setRecordViewers(res.data); }) .catch(() => {}); // Fetch persisted comments and map to FeedItem[] dataSource.find('sys_comment', { $filter: `threadId eq '${threadId}'`, $orderby: 'createdAt asc' }) .then((res: any) => { ``` **apps/console/src/components/RecordDetailView.tsx:80** * The `useEffect` dependency list includes `currentUser`, but `currentUser` is a new object literal each render, which will cause this effect to refetch presence/comments unnecessarily. Prefer depending on stable primitives (e.g., `currentUser.id`) or memoize `currentUser` with `useMemo`. ``` }) .catch(() => {}); }, [dataSource, objectName, pureRecordId, currentUser]); ```
